To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
integrins in the yolk cell and amnioseros.
integrins in the amniosiserosa and yoke cell are necessary for dorsal closure in the Drosophila embryo.

the yolk cell is an additional player in dorsal closure, integrins are required for three functions in the yolk cell and amnioserosal membranes, and integrin-extracelluar matrix interactions mediate cell-cell interactions in the amnion and yolk cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of integrins in epithelial cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions during Drosophiladorsal closure.
the role of cell adhesion molecules in morphogenesis and wound repair.
how epithelial morphogenesis is achieved and regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integrin function in dorsal closure is required for the formation of the amnion, the formation of the dorsal midline, and the formation of the epidermis.

the integrins and extracellular matrix are essential for dorsal closure and that they play multiple roles during morphogenesis, including cell attachment and adhesion, cell contraction, and cell migration.

integrins are required for the assembly of a provisional extracellular matrix, for the attachment of cells to the matrix, for the adhesion of cells to each other via the matrix, and for the contraction of the amniotic cell layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
integrins have novel functions in epithelial morphogenesis that are distinct from the roles of integrins during cell migration.

dorsal closure is not just a process of epithelial sheet closure, but also involves a novel mechanism of wound healing that requires the interaction of two cell layers and a novel extracellular matrix.
integrins play a role in the formation of an intermediate matrix and in the attachment of cells to this matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
integrins can have novel functions in cell-cell adhesion and that integrins can mediate interactions with the extracellular matrix in a cell-cell context.
integrins have a much wider repertoire of functions during epithelial morphogenesis than has been appreciated previously.
the yolk cell, a cell that is often ignored, plays a critical role in dorsal closure.
